title: A Textbook Remedy for Domain Shifts: Knowledge Priors for Medical Image Analysis

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model robustness using confounded datasets (NIH-sex, ISIC-sex) where disease classes are spuriously correlated with patient sex during training, and measuring the performance drop on an out-of-distribution test set where the correlation is reversed.

Evaluating model robustness using confounded datasets (NIH-age, ISIC-age) where disease classes are spuriously correlated with patient age (e.g., young vs. old) during training, and measuring the performance drop on an out-of-distribution test set where the correlation is reversed.

Evaluating model robustness using a confounded dataset (CheXpert-race) where disease classes are spuriously correlated with patient race (White, Black or African American) during training, and measuring the performance drop on an out-of-distribution test set where the correlation is reversed.

Evaluating model robustness using a confounded dataset (ISIC-color) where disease classes are spuriously correlated with patient skin color (light vs. dark based on the Fitzpatrick scale) during training, and measuring the performance drop on an out-of-distribution test set where the correlation is reversed.
